claim_updates.reason: This experiment is diagnostic for OECD/COINr pipeline ranking stability under sample-size variation, not a direct advancement of C-MEAS-VALID. Frozen decision_rule MIXED verdict: C1 PASS (raw features reproduce eta2=1.0), C2 PASS (hierarchy anchor eta2=0.0), C3 PASS (pipeline max eta2=0.999645 at n=20), C4 PASS (natural ranking preserved for tag_entropy both definitions at n=20), C5 PASS (Spearman=1.0 monotonic improvement, +55.95pp), C6 FAIL (canonical recipe agreement 55.95% < 80% threshold). The ranking instability is partially sample-size-dependent but not fully resolved at maximum available n=20. Audit PASS confirms all recomputed metrics match producer. C-MEAS-VALID retains EXPERIMENTAL status from prior valid experiments (decompression-normalization sub-thread); this experiment does not advance or falsify the broader measurement-validity claim.

product_action: DO_NOT_PROMOTE_RECIPE_DENSITY — canonical recipe ranking agreement (55.95%) is below the 80% stability threshold at maximum available sample size n=20; bootstrap CI 57.1% ± 49.5% confirms ranking is not reliably preserved. Product lane must use non-recipe density (100% ranking agreement per parent B2) and accept the eta2 reduction from recipe sampling. Full DOM testing (n=21-82) is still warranted as a final check but the n=20 plateau strongly suggests structural instability within this sample range.
next_question: Does the OECD/COINr pipeline preserve feature-weighted density ranking on full DOM elements (n=21-82 per task, not truncated-first-20) with richer element diversity — specifically, does canonical recipe ranking agreement reach the 80% threshold when the effective element count exceeds the 20-element truncation ceiling?
reason: Frozen conjunctive decision_rule evaluation: C1 PASS, C2 PASS, C3 PASS, C4 PASS, C5 PASS, NOT C6 → MIXED per spec.json verdict matrix. The sample-size effect is real and monotonic (Spearman=1.0 on 4 points, +55.95pp improvement from n=5 to n=20) but canonical recipe agreement plateaus at 55.95% at n=20 — well below the 80% threshold. Bootstrap variance (57.1% ± 49.5%) confirms ranking is not a stable property of this task set. The improvement from n=15 (50%) to n=20 (56%) is only +6pp over the last quintile, suggesting diminishing returns. Per-task recipe achieves 78.65% (close to 80% but not tested by frozen C6 which only requires canonical). The MIXED verdict means: ranking instability is partially sample-size-dependent but not resolved at maximum available n=20; recipe-sampling destabilization is structural within this sample range. Full DOM testing (n=21-82) is still warranted but the truncated-first-20 evidence strongly suggests the structural interpretation. Audit PASS confirms all recomputed metrics match producer; no discrepancies found.
